regulatory.product: chocolate or sugar products; cocoa, coffee and tea
regulatory.status: No ML set at time of opinion (2009)
regulatory.locator: text below Table 6; text below Table 12

exposure.statement: Highest cadmium concentrations among food commodities were detected in seaweed, fish and seafood, chocolate, and foods for special dietary uses.
Tolerable weekly intake (TWI) for cadmium established by the CONTAM Panel.
Mean exposure for adults across Europe is close to, or slightly exceeding, the TWI; vegetarians, children, smokers and residents of highly contaminated areas may exceed it about 2-fold.

Sugar and sugar products including chocolate (SAF-adjusted mean Cd 0.0264 mg/kg x median consumption 43 g/day) gives a category exposure of 1.135 µg Cd/day; chocolate subcategory contributes 0.0188 mg/kg of the 0.0264 adjusted category mean.
exposure.population: adult consumers, median across Member States

exposure.statement: Coffee, tea, cocoa expressed as liquid (dry concentration divided by 18) gives adjusted mean 0.0018 mg/kg x 601 g/day = 1.082 µg Cd/day; cocoa not separated.
exposure.population: adult consumers, median across Member States
exposure.locator: text preceding Table 20 (dilution factor 18) and Table 25 (p. 44)

exposure.statement: Chocolate consumption in the 1st French TDS: ovolactovegetarians mean 6.7 g/day (P95 26.1) vs general population 2.7 g/day (P95 14.3) (consumption, not exposure).
exposure.population: French ovolactovegetarians >15 y (n=74) vs general population (n=1474)

contradictions_with_stored_summary: Stored summary has no cocoa/chocolate occurrence values; it lists chocolate among high-Cd foods but omits the chocolate (mean 89.6 µg/kg, P95 300 µg/kg), dark vs milk (163.7 vs 25.3 µg/kg) and cocoa powder/bean (mean 177.6 µg/kg, P95 500, max 2075) statistics printed in Tables 6 and 12.
unresolved: Cocoa category 081 mixes cocoa powder and cocoa beans; cannot separate. Appendix definition of 02_3 also lists cocoa powder, so cocoa powder may be split across categories.
Specific Member State origin of chocolate/cocoa samples not reported; overlaps EFSA 2012 dataset (EFSA 2012 says this was a previous subset) and GEMS/Food European submissions.
